§01-001 JDK toolchain: javac, java, jshell, jpackage

6 Lessons 00m00s / 00m00s
Java Bytecode JVM Architecture `javac` Compiler Classpath Memory Management Command-Line Utilities.
CLI & Compilation Java SE 21 Developer: Command-line utilities
20m 45s

Deep dive into `javac`, `java`, classpath (`-cp`), and module options.

Official Documentation References
Oracle JDK 21 Tool Specifications: `javac` Options — Command-line syntax, `-cp` / `--class-path`, module path options (`-p`), and release targets.
Oracle JDK 21 Tool Specifications: `java` Standard Options — Standard VM options, system properties (`-D`), and class execution.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

The JDK CLI utilities (javac, java, jar, jshell, jpackage) provide the core compilation and execution toolchain independent of any IDE. javac compiles .java source code into platform-independent .class bytecode files, while java launches the Java Virtual Machine runtime.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Developer Source (.java) -> javac (compiler) -> Bytecode (.class) -> java (JVM process / JIT compiler) -> Host OS execution.

Key Code / CLI Example
javac -d out/ -cp "lib/*" src/App.java
java -cp "out:lib/*" com.example.App --release 21
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Neglecting the -d flag causes javac to output .class files next to .java source files in the source tree, breaking package directory matching.

Deep-dive with AI:
Watch on LinkedIn
CLI & Compilation Learning Java 17: How to build and execute Java programs
2m 47s

Practical walkthrough of compile-and-run workflow.

Official Documentation References
Oracle Java SE 21 Tools: Source-File Mode — Launching single-file source code programs without explicit compilation.
Oracle Java SE 21 Docs: Classpath Specification — How the compiler and launcher search for user classes and library archives.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

Java 11+ single-file source-code execution mode allows running a .java file directly with 'java App.java' without explicit prior javac compilation, compiling in-memory for fast prototyping and scripting.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

java App.java skips saving .class to disk; the JVM compiles the source in RAM and invokes the main method in a single step.

Key Code / CLI Example
// Run directly from terminal without explicit javac:
java src/com/example/QuickScript.java arg1 arg2
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Single-file mode only compiles the single target .java file; referencing other separate uncompiled .java files in the same directory will cause compilation errors unless pre-compiled.

Deep-dive with AI:
Watch on LinkedIn
JVM Memory Architecture Java Memory Management: Introduction to the garbage collector
2m 38s

Memory layout, role of the GC, and allocation.

Official Documentation References
Oracle HotSpot Virtual Machine Garbage Collection Tuning Guide — Generational memory layout, young/old generational hypothesis, and default ergonomics.
Oracle JVM SE 21 Specification: Runtime Data Areas — The pc register, Java virtual machine stacks, heap, and method area.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

The HotSpot Garbage Collector is an automatic memory management subsystem responsible for identifying and reclaiming heap memory occupied by unreachable objects, eliminating manual free() operations.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Objects are allocated in Heap memory. Thread execution frames live in Stack memory. When all GC roots (stack variables, static fields, JNI handles) lose their references to a heap object, it becomes eligible for collection.

Key Code / CLI Example
// Explicit System.gc() is only a hint and should NOT be used in production:
System.gc(); // Antipattern - triggers full STW (Stop-The-World) pause
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Assuming System.gc() forces immediate cleanup. It only triggers a hint to the JVM, frequently causing catastrophic Stop-The-World (STW) latency spikes.

Deep-dive with AI:
Watch on LinkedIn
JVM Memory Architecture Java Memory Management: Different generations on the heap
6m 3s

Generational hypothesis, Young Gen (Eden, S0, S1) and Old Gen.

Official Documentation References
Oracle HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Generations — Performance rationale for dividing the heap into young and tenured generations.
Oracle HotSpot GC Tuning Guide: Young Generation Sizing — Survivor space ratios (`-XX:SurvivorRatio`) and tenuring thresholds.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

HotSpot's Generational Garbage Collection partitions the heap based on the Weak Generational Hypothesis: most objects die shortly after allocation. The heap is split into Young Generation (Eden + Survivor spaces S0/S1) and Old (Tenured) Generation.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Allocation -> Eden -> (Minor GC survivors copy to S0 or S1, aging by 1 tenure threshold) -> Old Generation (when age exceeds -XX:MaxTenuringThreshold or survivor overflows).

Key Code / CLI Example
# JVM generational tuning flags:
java -XX:NewRatio=2 -XX:SurvivorRatio=8 -XX:MaxTenuringThreshold=15 -jar app.jar
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Premature tenuring: If survivor spaces are too small, short-lived objects spill directly into Old Gen, triggering frequent, expensive Major/Full GCs.

Deep-dive with AI:
Watch on LinkedIn
JVM Memory Architecture Java Memory Management: Heap size and heap dumps
4m 9s

Heap sizing flags (`-Xms`, `-Xmx`) and capturing heap dumps.

Official Documentation References
Oracle Java SE 21 Tools: Advanced GC Options — Flags including `-XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError` and `-XX:HeapDumpPath`.
Oracle Java SE 21 Tools: `jcmd` Utility — Generating live heap diagnostics and thread dumps via CLI.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

JVM heap sizing parameters control initial and maximum memory thresholds (-Xms and -Xmx). Diagnostic heap dumps (HPROF) capture complete object snapshots for analyzing memory leaks and OutOfMemoryError.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Setting -Xms == -Xmx avoids JVM runtime heap expansion/contraction overhead. Heap dump captures an instant memory freeze frame.

Key Code / CLI Example
java -Xms4g -Xmx4g -XX:+HeapDumpOnOutOfMemoryError -XX:HeapDumpPath=/var/dumps/oom.hprof -jar app.jar
# Capture live dump via CLI:

try (Stream<String> lines = Files.lines(Path.of("large.log"))) {
    lines.filter(l -> l.contains("ERROR"))
         .forEach(System.out::println);
} // Critical: try-with-resources closes the file channel
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Failing to close Files.lines() with try-with-resources causes file descriptor leaks that lock files on Windows and exhaust OS handles on Linux.

module com.example.service {

    exports com.example.service.api;
}

Cyclic dependencies between modules: JPMS strictly forbids circular module references at compile time and runtime.

Core Definition & Architectural Role

requires declares a dependency on another module. requires transitive re-exports the dependency so downstream consumers inherit it. exports exposes a package to consumers.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

exports makes public types in that package visible to others. requires transitive creates transitive dependency chains (implied readability).

module com.example.core {
    exports com.example.core.model;           // Visible to all
    exports com.example.core.internal to com.example.admin; // Qualified export
    requires transitive java.logging;         // Downstream modules also read java.logging
}
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Exporting a package that returns types from a non-transitive required module: clients cannot compile because they lack readability of the return type.

}

Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

A canonical Builder is implemented as a public static class Builder inside the target class, with a private target constructor that copies validated values from the builder.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

The builder holds mutable transient state. The target object copies fields immutably and validates invariants inside build().

Key Code / CLI Example
public class NutritionFacts {
    private final int calories, fat;
    private NutritionFacts(Builder b) {
        this.calories = b.calories;
        this.fat = b.fat;
    }
    public static class Builder {
        private int calories, fat;
        public Builder calories(int c) { this.calories = c; return this; }
        public Builder fat(int f) { this.fat = f; return this; }
        public NutritionFacts build() { return new NutritionFacts(this); }
    }
}
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Validating parameters in builder setter methods instead of build(): subsequent setter calls or concurrent modifications can invalidate early checks.

Memory Leaks & Obsolete References Java Memory Management: Eligible for garbage collection
1m 39s

Eliminating obsolete object references.

Official Documentation References
Oracle Java SE 21 Docs: Reachability Types — Strong, soft, weak, and phantom reachability.
📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

An object is eligible for garbage collection as soon as it becomes unreachable through any chain of strong references originating from GC Roots.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

GC Roots include: 1) Active local variables in thread call stacks, 2) Static class variables, 3) Active JNI pointers. If no path exists from roots, it is dead.

Key Code / CLI Example
Object obj = new Object(); // Reachable via local variable root
obj = null;                // Eligible for GC: no live roots retain it
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Believing circular references prevent GC: if Object A references B and B references A, but neither is reachable from GC Roots, BOTH are reclaimed.

Official Documentation References

📝Comprehensive Study Notes & Mental ModelQuick Review
Expand NotesCollapse
Core Definition & Architectural Role

Effective Java Item 7: Eliminate obsolete object references. Memory leaks in Java occur when objects that will never be used again remain unintentionally reachable from live GC roots.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Common leak vectors: unbounded static collections, unclosed streams/sockets, lingering event listeners/callbacks, and un-nulled elements in custom array-backed data structures.

Key Code / CLI Example
public Object pop() {
    if (size == 0) throw new EmptyStackException();
    Object result = elements[--size];
    elements[size] = null; // Clear obsolete reference to allow GC!
    return result;
}
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Failing to unregister listeners or retaining cache keys strongly: use WeakHashMap or evicting cache libraries (Caffeine) instead of raw HashMap for caching.

}

Relying on ordinal() for database persistence: reordering enum constants shifts their numeric ordinals, silently corrupting stored data.

Core Definition & Architectural Role

Enums in Java are full-fledged classes that can have instance fields, constructors (private by default), methods, and constant-specific class bodies implementing abstract methods.

🧠Under-The-Hood Mental Model

Constant-specific method body: each enum constant acts as an anonymous subclass overriding the base enum method.

Key Code / CLI Example
public enum Operation {
    PLUS("+")  { public double apply(double x, double y) { return x + y; } },
    MINUS("-") { public double apply(double x, double y) { return x - y; } };
    
    private final String symbol;
    Operation(String symbol) { this.symbol = symbol; }
    public abstract double apply(double x, double y);
}
⚠️Common Pitfall & Production Gotcha

Declaring mutable fields in an enum: enum constants are effectively global singletons, so mutable state creates thread-safety hazards and race conditions.
